gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 15-inch Air's battery is 66.5 Wh and Apple's 18-hour streaming figure implies about 3.7 W average draw, so a 4.5 W bus-powered screen more than doubles the drain (about 8 hours on that arithmetic).
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's roundup, thisUSB, WorkCocoon, DeskExpander and Dealectric's two cited pages. thisUSB gives monitor draws (about 5-10 W) and says 'a laptop can usually supply that'; Macworld only lists 'Laptop battery drain' as an espresso Pro con; WorkCocoon says the Air has 'less power headroom' with no figure. None gives the Air's 66.5 Wh battery, a runtime figure, or the fact that MagSafe leaves both video ports free. The per-chip display counts, the M3 lid-closed rule, macOS lacking MST, and DisplayLink's Screen Recording and HDCP limits are already on thisUSB or Dealectric's pages, so they are not the gap.
decides: It confirms a single 1080p screen (Duex Max DS class, 4.5 W on Mobile Pixels' Duex Max spec page) as the pick for an Air used on battery, and it pushes the Trio 3 Pro to a plugged-in setup: Macworld (Simon Jary) says its screens cannot reach full brightness on laptop power and it weighs 4.13 lb against the Air's 3.3 lb. The Air's separate MagSafe port means two no-driver screens plus charging works on M4/M5 without a hub. On M2 and M3 the plan stops at one added screen with the lid open (Apple), so a two-screen extender there needs the driver route.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch (M2, 2023) external displays
findings.value: One external display with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz, with the built-in display at full native resolution
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section; also lists 'Native DisplayPort output over USB-C'.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch (M3, 2024) external displays
findings.value: One external display up to 6K 60Hz with the lid open; 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display with up to 5K resolution at 60Hz'
findings.note: Apple's words. An attached or stacked extender mounts on the open lid, so the second-display mode cannot be used with one.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch (M4, 2025) external displays
findings.value: Up to two external displays with up to 6K resolution at 60Hz, with the built-in display at full native resolution
findings.note: Also 'Support for native DisplayPort 1.4 output over USB-C'.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch (M5, current) external displays
findings.value: Supports up to two external displays (two up to 6K 60Hz or 4K 144Hz); 'Simultaneously supports the built-in display at full native resolution'
findings.note: Current 15-inch model lists the Apple M5 chip.

findings.label: Video-capable ports and charging port on every 15-inch Air (M2, M3, M4, M5)
findings.value: Two Thunderbolt (USB-C) ports with support for charging and DisplayPort, plus a separate MagSafe 3 charging port
findings.note: Same port list read on 111346 (M2), 118552 (M3) and apple.com/macbook-air/specs (M5). Inference: no-driver screens top out at two (one per port), and charging through MagSafe leaves both ports free.

findings.label: MacBook Air 15-inch battery and Apple's runtime claims
findings.value: 66.5 Wh; up to 18 hours video streaming; up to 15 hours wireless web
findings.note: Apple footnote: tested January 2026 on preproduction 15-inch M5 units, brightness 8 clicks from bottom, 1080p streaming in Safari on Wi-Fi. Battery figure read for the M5 model only.

findings.label: Power consumption and body size
findings.note: The page is for the Duex Max, not the DS revision; a DS-specific figure was not read. The page lists no weight or laptop fit range.

findings.label: Derived: Air 15 runtime with a 4.5 W bus-powered screen
findings.value: About 8.1 hours against Apple's 18 (streaming test); about 7.4 hours against 15 (web test)
findings.note: My arithmetic, not a measurement: 66.5 Wh / 18 h = 3.69 W implied average; + 4.5 W = 8.19 W; 66.5 / 8.19 = 8.1 h. Web: 66.5 / 15 = 4.43 W; + 4.5 = 8.93 W; 7.4 h. Ignores the Mac's extra work driving a second display, so real runtime would be lower.

findings.label: Derived: Duex Max body against the Air 15 lid
findings.value: 12.6 x 8.9 in screen body sits inside the 13.40 x 9.35 in Air footprint
findings.note: Apple width 13.40 in, depth 9.35 in, weight 3.3 lb (same on the M2, M3 and M5 pages). Duex dimensions are from the non-DS spec page above. Not a maker fit statement.

findings.label: Derived: pixel density, 14.1-inch 1080p screen against the Air's panel
findings.note: Apple: 15.3-inch, 2880 x 1864 at 224 ppi, 500 nits. My arithmetic: sqrt(1920^2 + 1080^2) / 14.1 = 156 ppi, using the size and resolution on Mobile Pixels' Duex Max spec page.

findings.label: Video path on a Mac (Macworld, Simon Jary, 2 Apr 2026)
findings.value: Two included USB-C cables, one per screen; 'you need to install the software so that your can run both screens from the single cable connection'; manual quoted: 'if your laptop has two DP enabled USB-C ports ... driver installation is not necessary'
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld
findings.note: Jary tested on a 14-inch MacBook Pro and writes 'an M1/M2/M3 Pro/Max or any M4/M5 MacBook should be fine'. He names plain M1 and M2 as single-monitor Macs but not the M3 Air's lid-open limit, which Apple's page above supplies.

findings.label: Power and weight (Macworld, Simon Jary)
findings.value: Screens 'can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'; a power adapter on the Trio passes up to 65 W to the laptop; 4.13 lb (1.9 kg)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review - Macworld
findings.note: My arithmetic: 4.13 lb is 125% of the Air 15's 3.3 lb (Apple). Jary says it works best with 'four super-strong magnets' on the MacBook lid.

findings.label: Mac display driver (maker's page)
findings.value: Graphics Driver 4.1.0 for macOS 14 and later; 'DO NOT plug the Mobile Pixels Inc Device into your mac before executing the driver installation'
findings.source_title: 2023 Trio Series: Mac Display Driver - Mobile Pixels
findings.note: Page covers Trio Series 2nd and 3rd Gen. It does not name the driver's underlying technology, permissions or limitations.

findings.label: Apple on magnets and Mac notebook sleep
findings.value: A Mac notebook 'might sleep unexpectedly' when a magnet is 'under the computer or on its palm rest'
findings.source_title: Magnets can cause Mac notebooks to sleep - Apple Support (archived)
findings.note: Archived article, published 4 Aug 2023, no longer updated. Extender magnets go on the back of the lid, which is not a location Apple names, so this is context only and not evidence of a problem.
